storyboard.ears: The Great Barrier Reef is bleaching again, and recovery takes longer than the gaps.
The reef suffered 3 bleaching events this decade, turning a rare crisis into a recurring one.
storyboard.eyes: substance: coral turning bleached white; cause: Data pours steaming hot water over the side; the hot plume sinks onto a coral head and it turns white
storyboard.evidence: Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) | Great Barrier Reef mass bleaching events per decade | https://aims.gov.au/sites/default/files/2024-04/FINAL-Aerial%20Bleaching%20GBR2024Report_AIMS_Final_15Apr2024_0.pdf | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: The gap between bleachings shrank to 2 years, leaving little time for damaged coral to rebuild.
storyboard.eyes: substance: living coral branches; cause: Data plants a coral fragment for each year of recovery and each one grows into a branch
storyboard.evidence: Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) | Years between Great Barrier Reef mass bleaching events | https://aims.gov.au/sites/default/files/2024-04/FINAL-Aerial%20Bleaching%20GBR2024Report_AIMS_Final_15Apr2024_0.pdf | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: Recovery typically needs 10 years, so the next bleaching wave can arrive before healing finishes.
storyboard.evidence: Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) / NOAA Coral Reef Watch | Coral recovery time vs time actually between bleaching events | https://aims.gov.au | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: Repeated bleaching can erase a decade of reef recovery before it finishes.
